newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine deputies make progress in budget reading.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine deputies make progress in budget reading.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament made some progress on the much-delayed 1997 budget on Tuesday, approving the key revenues and expenditures plans at a second reading ahead of a third and final reading planned for Thursday.
Deputies approved revenues of 22.39 billion hryvnias ($12.1 billion) and expenditures of 28.12 billion hryvnias as proposed by Nikolai Azarov, head of the budget committee.
Parliament ruled that 3.33 billion hryvnias of the projected deficit would be covered using domestic sources of cash and 2.4 billion hryvnias from foreign credits.

But it rejected a proposal by the budget and financing committees to use only funds from the Treasury bill market to cover the deficit on the domestic side, allowing the possibility that the central bank would cover part of the deficit.
Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov said his ministry had relied on only one central bank emission this year, but did not say how much it was or what it was for.
Official data show the bank issued 32.9 million hryvnias towards covering the deficit between January and April while 1.573 billion hryvnias came from T-bills.
Passing this year's budget is a key condition for Ukraine to qualify for a $2.5-$3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility from the International Monetary Fund.
